fundamentals.name: Lumentum Holdings Inc.
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: Lumentum Holdings Inc. manufactures and sells optical and photonic products in the Americas, the Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. It operates through two segments, Cloud & Networking and Industrial Tech. The Cloud & Networking segment offers optical and photonic chips, components, modules, and subsystems supplied to cloud data center operators, AI/ML infrastructure providers, and network equipment manufacturer customers that are building cloud data centers and network infrastructures. Its Industrial Tech segment provides short-pulse solid-state lasers, kilowatt-class fiber lasers, diode lasers, and gas lasers that serves the semiconductor device, solar cell, display, and electric vehicle and battery manufacturing markets. The company was incorporated in 2015 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.

judgment.summary: Strong growth and profitability are offset by a high valuation and significant debt.
judgment.earningsRecap: Last quarter beat EPS estimates by 4.6%; next earnings date is 2026-05-05.
positives: Revenue growth 90.1% YoY and analyst estimates for current Q (236.6%) and FY (300.7%) indicate very strong top-line expansion.
Operating margin of 21.8% and profit margin of 17.7% show healthy profitability.
Return on equity at 22.8% is robust.
PEG ratio of 0.63 suggests the stock may be undervalued relative to its growth prospects.
negatives: Trailing P/E of 158.16 and Forward P/E of 49.98 indicate a very high valuation.
Price/Sales (TTM) of 28.28 and Price/Book of 76.30 are also very high.
Debt/Equity ratio of 111.44 and total debt exceeding total cash suggest a leveraged balance sheet.
Free cash flow of $93.35M TTM appears low relative to market cap and debt.

news.paragraph: Lumentum Holdings (LITE) has seen its shares surge significantly, with a 13.7% jump reported on June 2nd, contributing to a broader optics rally. This price action follows speculation about potential benefits from a reported US$2 billion Nvidia investment and Google's increased AI spending plans. While the company recently beat its Q1 EPS estimates, the valuation metrics suggest that much of this positive news may already be priced in.
